seoTitle: Fix Namecheap Redirect Not Working: Full Guide
metaDescription: Namecheap domain redirect not working? Learn how to properly set up domain forwarding, choose 301 vs 302, and fix common DNS-related redirect issues.
intro: When a Namecheap domain redirect isn't working, it's usually down to how the forwarding is configured rather than a fault with Namecheap itself. This guide covers setting up domain forwarding correctly, choosing the right redirect type, and troubleshooting propagation or conflicting record issues.

steps.heading: Open domain forwarding settings
steps.body: Log in to Namecheap and find the domain forwarding or redirect option under your domain's management settings.

steps.heading: Set up the redirect destination
steps.body: Enter the URL you want visitors to be sent to when they reach your domain.

steps.heading: Choose the correct redirect type
steps.body: Select either a 301 (permanent) or 302 (temporary) redirect depending on whether the change is meant to be lasting or short-term.

steps.heading: Check for conflicting DNS records
steps.body: Review your DNS records for entries that might conflict with the redirect, since leftover A or CNAME records can prevent forwarding from working.

steps.heading: Allow propagation and retest
steps.body: Give the changes time to propagate, then test the domain again in a fresh browser session to confirm the redirect is functioning.

faq.question: Should I use a 301 or 302 redirect?
faq.answer: A 301 redirect is best for permanent moves, while a 302 is better suited to temporary redirects that you plan to change later.

faq.question: Why isn't my Namecheap redirect working right away?
faq.answer: DNS propagation delays are a common cause, so it's worth waiting before assuming the redirect setup itself is broken.

faq.question: Can conflicting DNS records break a redirect?
faq.answer: Yes, leftover or conflicting A and CNAME records can interfere with forwarding, so those need to be reviewed and cleaned up.

faq.question: Does redirecting a domain affect its SEO?
faq.answer: A 301 redirect generally passes SEO value to the destination, while a 302 does not carry the same permanence for search engines.
